text:
Through the infinite melodies of their speech, which set in motion the various modes of the Wheel <note>the Wheel of Dharma</note>, I too shall enter deeply into those teachings by the power of my intellect. I shall engage with all future eons in a single instant; I shall practice by entering into the measurements of all eons of the three times <note>past, present, and future</note> in but a fraction of a moment.

In a single instant, I shall behold those lions among men who travel through the three times. By the power of a liberation that is like a magical illusion, I shall always enter into their sphere of activity. I shall realize the array of pure lands of the three times upon a single atom. In that way, I shall enter into the arrays of the lands of the Victors in every direction without exception.

I shall approach all those Protectors, the lamps of the world who are yet to come, as they gradually attain enlightenment, turn the Wheel, and demonstrate the final peace of <term>Nirvana</term> <gloss>the cessation of suffering</gloss>. 

By the power of miracles that are swift in all ways, the power of the vehicle that is a door in all ways, the power of conduct that possesses qualities in all ways, and the power of loving-kindness that is all-pervading; by the power of merit that is virtuous in all ways, the power of wisdom that is unattached, and the powers of insight, skillful means, and meditative concentration, I shall perfectly accomplish the powers of enlightenment.

I shall completely purify the power of karma, I shall thoroughly crush the power of the mental afflictions, I shall render the power of the <term>maras</term> <gloss>demonic obstructions</gloss> powerless, and I shall complete all the powers of Samantabhadra’s conduct <note>the conduct of the Always Good</note>.

I shall purify oceans of lands, I shall liberate oceans of sentient beings, I shall clearly see oceans of Dharma, and I shall deeply realize oceans of primordial wisdom. I shall purify oceans of conduct, I shall fulfill oceans of aspirations, I shall make offerings to oceans of Buddhas, and I shall practice without weariness throughout oceans of eons. 

<summary>This page contains verses from the Prayer of Good Conduct expressing the practitioner's aspiration to master time, enter pure lands, and fulfill the vast deeds of a Bodhisattva. It emphasizes the use of spiritual powers to overcome afflictions and serve beings across infinite eons.</summary>
<keywords>Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra, Nirvana, three times, eons, spiritual powers, Wheel of Dharma, pure lands</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>in all worlds. Just as a lotus is not soiled by water, and the sun and moon move unhindered through the sky, so shall I act without attachment. Throughout the extent of the lands and in all directions, I shall completely pacify the suffering of the lower realms. I shall place all beings in happiness and act for the benefit of every living creature.

I shall bring the conduct of enlightenment to full completion and act in harmony with the diverse behaviors of sentient beings. Showing the way of Noble Conduct <note>The Sanskrit title is Bhadracarya, often called the King of Prayers.</note>, I shall practice throughout all future eons. May I always be in the company of those whose actions are similar to my own. Through body, speech, and also mind, may we practice our deeds and aspirations as one. 

May I always meet those friends who wish to help me and who clearly demonstrate Noble Conduct. May I never disappoint them. I shall always behold the Victors, the Protectors surrounded by the Children of the Buddha <note>original: "sangs rgyas sras," referring to Bodhisattvas</note>. Without ever growing weary throughout all future eons, I shall make vast offerings to them.

Holding the sublime Dharma of the Victors and making the conduct of enlightenment shine everywhere, I shall purify the Noble Conduct and practice it throughout all future eons. Even while circling through all states of existence, I shall find inexhaustible merit and wisdom. May I become an inexhaustible treasury of all qualities: means, primordial wisdom, meditative concentration, and total liberation.

Upon a single atom are lands as numerous as all atoms, and in those lands sit inconceivable Buddhas. In the midst of these Children of the Buddha, I shall behold them as I practice the conduct of enlightenment. In this way, in every direction without exception, even in the space of a single hair, there are oceans of Buddhas of the three times, oceans of lands, and oceans of eons; I shall enter and practice among them.

With each word possessing the sound of an ocean of qualities, the pure melody of all the Victors, a voice that accords with the inclinations of all beings, I shall always engage with the speech of the Buddha. The Victors who have gone in the three times...

<summary>This page contains verses from the King of Aspiration Prayers, focusing on the Bodhisattva's commitment to benefit all beings across all worlds and future eons. It emphasizes the purity of conduct and the infinite nature of the Buddha's presence and speech.</summary>
<keywords>Bodhisattva vow, Noble Conduct, Bhadracarya, merit and wisdom, three times, Buddha fields, compassion</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>if they recite it, they will quickly and completely be purified of all <note>sins, including the five heinous crimes mentioned in the previous verse</note>. They will be endowed with primordial wisdom <term>jnana</term>, a beautiful form, the physical marks of excellence, a noble lineage, and a radiant complexion. Many demons and heretics <term>tirthika</term> <gloss>non-Buddhist extremists</gloss> will not be able to overcome them. They will be honored throughout all the three worlds.

They will quickly go to the foot of the king of trees <note>the Bodhi tree where enlightenment is attained</note>. Having gone there, they will sit for the benefit of all sentient beings. They will attain awakening <term>bodhi</term> as a Buddha, turn the wheel of the doctrine, and subdue all the hosts of demons <term>mara</term>.

The full ripening <note>the karmic result</note> of any person who holds, teaches, or reads this Prayer of Excellent Conduct <term>Bhadracarya Pranidhana</term> is known only by the Buddhas. Do not have any doubt regarding the supreme awakening.

Just as the hero Manjushri knows, and Samantabhadra knows likewise, I train myself to follow their examples and dedicate all these virtues to that end. With that dedication which is praised as supreme by all the Victors <term>Jina</term> <gloss>Buddhas</gloss> who have gone in the three times <note>past, present, and future</note>, I dedicate all these roots of my virtue toward excellent conduct.

When it is time for me to die, may all my obscurations be cleared away. Having seen the Boundless Light <term>Amitabha</term> appearing directly before me, may I go to that pure land of Bliss <term>Sukhavati</term>.

Having gone there, may all these prayers be manifested without exception. May I fulfill them all completely and benefit sentient beings for as long as the world remains.

In that beautiful and joyful mandala of the Victor, may I be born from a very beautiful and supreme lotus. May I receive a direct prophecy of my future enlightenment there from the Victorious One, Boundless Light.

Having received that prophecy, may I perform many benefits for sentient beings in the ten directions through the power of my intellect, using many hundreds of millions of emanations.

Through whatever small amount of virtue I have accumulated by reciting the Prayer of Excellent Conduct, may all the virtuous prayers of the world be fulfilled in a single instant.

<summary>This page concludes the benefits of reciting the Bhadracarya Pranidhana and outlines the practitioner's aspiration to be reborn in Sukhavati to achieve enlightenment for the sake of all beings.</summary>
<keywords>Bhadracarya Pranidhana, Samantabhadra, Manjushri, Amitabha, Sukhavati, dedication of merit, Bodhi tree, prophecy of enlightenment</keywords>

{D4377} In the language of India: <term>Arya Bhadracarya Pranidhana Raja</term> <gloss>The Noble King of Prayers for Excellent Conduct</gloss>. In the language of Tibet: <term>Phagpa Zangpo Chöpe Mönlam gyi Gyalpo</term>.

I pay homage to the noble Manjushri, who has the form of a youth.

To all the lions among men <note>an epithet for the Buddhas</note>, the ones who have gone to the bliss of the three times in the worlds of the ten directions, I pay homage to every single one of them with a devoted body, speech, and mind.

By the power of the prayer for excellent conduct, I manifest all the Victors directly in my mind. With bodies as numerous as the atoms of the world, I bow deeply and pay homage to all the Victors.

Upon every single atom sit as many Buddhas as there are atoms, each residing in the midst of the Sons of the Buddha <note>the Bodhisattvas</note>. In this way, I realize that the entire expanse of phenomena <note>the <term>dharmadhatu</term></note> is completely filled with Victors.

With oceans of inexhaustible praise, through the sounds of an ocean of melodic branches, I proclaim the qualities of all the Victors and praise all those who have gone to bliss.

With the finest flowers and the finest garlands, with music, scented oils, and the best parasols, with the finest lamps and the best incense, I make offerings to those Victors.

With the finest garments and the best fragrances, with mounds of powdered incense as high as Mount Meru, and with all types of superior and exalted arrangements, I make offerings to those Victors.

Whatever offerings are unsurpassed and vast, I offer them with devotion to all the Victors. By the power of my faith in excellent conduct, I pay homage and make offerings to all the Victors.

Whatever negative actions I have committed with my body, speech, and likewise my mind, under the influence of desire, hatred, and ignorance, I individually confess every one of them.

In whatever merit belongs to the Victors of the ten directions, the Sons of the Buddha, the Solitary Realizers, those in training, those beyond training, and all migrating beings, I rejoice in all of it.

To those who are the lamps of the worlds in the ten directions...

<summary>This page contains the opening verses of the King of Prayers, a fundamental Mahayana text focusing on the Seven-Limb Practice including prostration, offering, confession, and rejoicing. It establishes the practitioner's intent to honor all Buddhas across all space and time through visualized worship.</summary>
<keywords>King of Prayers, Samantabhadra, Bodhisattva conduct, Seven-Limb Practice, prostration, offering, confession, rejoicing, Manjushri</keywords>

Those lamps of the worlds <note>referring to the Buddhas</note>, who have traveled the stages of awakening and attained non-attachment, I urge all those protectors to turn the supreme wheel of Dharma. To those who intend to demonstrate their passing into final peace <term>nirvana</term>, I join my palms in prayer and entreat them to remain for as many eons as there are atoms in the world, for the benefit and happiness of all living beings. Whatever slight merit I have gathered through prostrating, offering, confessing, rejoicing, urging, and praying, I dedicate it all toward the attainment of complete awakening.

May the Buddhas of the past and those currently residing in the worlds of the ten directions be honored. May those who have not yet arrived quickly fulfill their intentions and reach awakening through the successive stages. May all the world realms in the ten directions become vast and utterly pure. May they be filled with conquerors <term>jinas</term> who have gone to the foot of the king of awakening trees <note>the Bodhi tree</note>, and with the children of the Buddhas <term>bodhisattvas</term>.

May as many sentient beings as exist in the ten directions always be healthy and happy. May the spiritual goals of all living beings be met in accordance with the Dharma, and may their hopes be fulfilled. As I practice the conduct of awakening <term>bodhicharya</term>, may I remember my past lives in all states of existence. In all my successive lives, through death, transition, and birth, may I always maintain my monastic vows <term>pravrajya</term>.

Following in the footsteps of all the conquerors, may I bring the Good Conduct <note>referring to the Samantabhadra-charya-pranidhana</note> to perfection. May I always practice a stainless and pure discipline, never failing and remaining without flaw. In the languages of the gods, the <term>nagas</term> <gloss>serpent spirits</gloss>, and the <term>yakshas</term> <gloss>nature spirits</gloss>, in the languages of the <term>kumbhandas</term> <gloss>spirits</gloss> and of humans, and in as many sounds as are made by all living beings, I shall teach the Dharma in every tongue.

By that, may I be diligent in the perfections <term>paramitas</term> and never forget the mind of awakening <term>bodhichitta</term>. May whatever misdeeds and obscurations I have accumulated be completely purified without exception. Freed from karma, mental afflictions, and the works of the demon <term>Mara</term>, I shall act in the world...

<summary>This page contains verses from the Prayer of Good Conduct, focusing on the Seven-Limb Prayer and aspirations for future lives. The speaker vows to teach the Dharma in all languages and to maintain pure discipline until achieving awakening.</summary>
<keywords>Samantabhadra, Seven-Limb Prayer, Bodhichitta, Dharma Wheel, Nirvana, Paramitas, Monasticism</keywords>

I will fulfill without exception all the various prayers for the conduct of awakening belonging to the Victorious Ones who have gone to bliss, by awakening through the <term>Bhadracarya</term> <gloss>Excellent Conduct</gloss>.

The eldest son of all the Victorious Ones is called by the name <term>Samantabhadra</term> <gloss>Universal Goodness</gloss>. In order to practice in a way equal to that wise one, I dedicate all these virtues.

May my body, speech, and mind be pure; may my conduct and even the realms be utterly pure. Just as the dedication of the wise and excellent one is, may I also become equal to him.

In order to practice the excellent virtue in every way, I shall practice the prayer of <term>Manjushri</term> <gloss>Gentle Glory, the Bodhisattva of Wisdom</gloss>. Without becoming weary through all future eons, I will fulfill those actions without exception.

May there be no limit to my conduct. May there be no measure to my qualities. By remaining within immeasurable conduct, I shall know all their miraculous manifestations.

As far as the ends of space reach, so also are sentient beings without end; as far as the ends of karma and mental afflictions reach, so also is the end of my prayer.

One might offer the infinite realms of the ten directions, adorned with jewels, to the Victorious Ones. One might also offer the supreme joys of gods and humans for as many eons as there are atoms in those realms. However, whoever hears this king of dedications and is greatly inspired toward supreme awakening, generating faith even just once, produces a merit that is more supreme and holy.

Whoever makes this prayer of <term>Bhadracarya</term> will abandon all lower realms of existence. Such a person has abandoned bad companions and will quickly see the Buddha <term>Amitabha</term> <gloss>Infinite Light</gloss>.

They obtain excellent gains and live in happiness. Even in this human life, things will go well for them. In a short time, they will become just like <term>Samantabhadra</term> himself.

Even the five sins of immediate retribution <note>These are five particularly heavy negative actions: killing one's father, killing one's mother, killing an Arhat, drawing the blood of a Buddha with ill intent, and creating a schism in the Sangha.</note> committed under the power of ignorance will be <unclear>purified</unclear> by someone who recites this <term>Bhadracarya</term>...

<summary>This page contains verses from the Prayer of Excellent Conduct (Bhadracarya), emphasizing the dedication of merit and the aspiration to emulate the Bodhisattvas Samantabhadra and Manjushri. It describes the vast merit gained from this prayer and its power to purify even the heaviest negative karmas.</summary>
<keywords>Samantabhadra, Manjushri, Bhadracarya, merit dedication, awakening, Amitabha, five sins of immediate retribution</keywords>
